structure: New York State K-8 Social Studies Framework (revised Feb 2017). Front matter (cover/contents, u1-u69) then Part 'Grades K-4': a K-4 vertical-articulation table of Social Studies Practices (columns C4..C8 = K,1,2,3,4; first-column cell = practice strand Gathering/Chronological/Comparison/Geographic/Economics/Civic, applies to K-4). Each grade K-4 section has: grade divider page, Common Core ELA & Literacy standards (Reading/Writing/Speaking and Listening; backup), 'Grade N: Social Studies Practices' (strands A-F, numbered practice statements, grade specific), and the grade course (title 'Grade N: <name>', overview narrative, then 5-10 Key Ideas per grade). K-3 are organized by unifying-theme headings (Individual Development and Cultural Identity; Civic Ideals and Practices; Geography, Humans, and the Environment; Time, Continuity, and Change; Economic Systems; plus Development, Movement, and Interaction of Cultures and Creation, Expansion, and Interaction of Economic Systems in grade 3). Key Ideas are coded N.n (K.1, 1.2, 4.7), Conceptual Understandings N.na (K.1a, 4.7b), each followed by a 'Students will ...' content specification (examples). Grade 4 has a Unifying Themes x Key Ideas alignment table (empty cells, marks lost in extraction) and Key Ideas 4.1-4.7 written as 'N.n TITLE: description (Standards: ..; Themes: ..)'. Part 'Grades 5-8': Common Core literacy standards in History/Social Studies (backup, 5-8), then a vertical-articulation table of Social Studies Practices for Grades 5-8 (data columns C4,C5,C6,C7 = grades 5,6,7,8 although the header cell for Grade 8 is C8). Grades 5, 6, 7, 8 each have a divider page, 'Grade N: Social Studies Practices' (A-F), a Unifying Themes aligned to Key Ideas table (no K-8 data in cells beyond theme names), and the course (Grade 5 Western Hemisphere 5.1-5.7; Grade 6 Eastern Hemisphere 6.1-6.7; Grade 7 US & NY I 7.1-7.8; Grade 8 US & NY II 8.1-8.9) with Key Idea (N.n), Conceptual Understandings (N.na), and 'Students will...' content specifications (examples). Grades 7 and 8 share one introductory narrative page (u1846-u1851). All content is grade-level (course = null); no separate named courses in this file.
